title: Antiblockade Quantum Batteries
abstract: Blockade, a phenomenon in which one particle hinders the transport of another, constitutes a core research topic in mesoscopic and microscopic physics. Benefiting from the unique single-particle characteristics, it underpins versatile applications spanning from quantum computation to quantum metrology. Nevertheless, in the context of quantum energy?storage devices, i.e., quantum batteries (QBs), blockade triggered by the intrinsic level splitting is in turn detrimental to energy accumulation. Here we propose an antiblockade charging protocol enabled by deliberately engineering a bright-dark interaction. Rooted in a manifold of equally-spaced dressed-dark states, this elaborate configuration opens up a new charging channel facilitating an antiblockade energy flow and outperforms the Rabi-split blockade design with at least a 20-fold enhancement in energy storage. Additionally, we further illustrate the achievement of superextensive (quadratic) charging characteristic by operating the system in the bad-cavity limit. In view of its inherent generality, our scheme offers a universal and feasible pathway toward high-performance quantum energy architectures.
summary: This paper introduces an antiblockade charging protocol for quantum batteries by engineering a bright-dark interaction within a three-level system. This novel protocol circumvents the energy-limiting blockade effect, leading to significantly enhanced energy storage capacity. The scheme is shown to be robust and capable of achieving superradiant power scaling in the bad-cavity limit.
main_problem: The primary challenge is overcoming the energy accumulation limitation in Quantum Batteries (QBs) caused by the inherent blockade effect.
main_result: The proposed antiblockade charging protocol, enabled by engineering a bright-dark interaction, significantly outperforms traditional blockade designs, achieving at least a 20-fold enhancement in energy storage.
method: The analysis uses non-Hermitian Hamiltonians and steady-state solution derivations to model the charging dynamics in the presence of engineered coupling.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a V-type three-level QB cell ensemble coupled to a bosonic charger, analyzed in the bright and dark state basis.
key_observables: Steady-state energy storage ($E_s$), mean charging power ($P(t)$), and the second-order correlation function ($g^{(2)}(	au)$).

The key regimes include the resonant scenario ($\omega_c = \omega_0$), the blockade ($\Delta=0$), and the antiblockade ($\Delta

main_assumptions: The analysis is simplified by restricting to the resonant scenario and retaining only lowest-order excitations for energy storage calculations.
figures_summary:
Figures illustrate energy diagrams comparing blockade ($\Delta=0$) vs. antiblockade ($\Delta

paper_structure: The paper introduces the blockade problem, proposes the antiblockade charging protocol via bright-dark coupling, derives the enhanced energy storage using non-Hermitian methods, and demonstrates superradiant power scaling in the bad-cavity limit.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses energy storage limitations in quantum devices by leveraging engineered quantum interference (bright-dark coupling) to create an antiblockade channel, which is highly relevant to cavity QED and open quantum system dynamics.
